statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 9% (low), Stress 51% (elevated), Confidence 89% (high), dominant mode normal. The three-hour lower-low sequence has stopped and price is compressing above the 31,003.75 session low.
recommendation: Tail at 9% remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON and green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The narrow evidence-based danger window spans 13:00Z to 15:00Z, covering the 13:30Z US cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global September finals and September ISM Services at 14:00Z. Stress at 51% stays elevated and describes a difficult but recoverable environment; it does not alter the Tail-derived mapping.
headline: Tail eases to 9% as the three-hour lower-low sequence stops with no new low since 31,003.75 and price compressing into a 17.5-point band, while Stress falls to 51% on the verified G7 100-million-barrel release and WTI below 90
body:
The overnight question an hour ago was whether a third successive lower low was the start of a directional path. Eighteen to twenty minutes of fresh five-minute data answer it, and the answer argues for a slightly lower Tail rather than a higher one. NQZ26 prints 31,041.50 at 07:20:51Z against a 31,061.75 prior close, a decline of 20.25 points or 0.065%. The session low remains 31,003.75 and the session high remains 31,221.25, a range of 217.5 points or 0.70%, with that high now unretested for roughly six hours.

The decisive evidence is what the 07:00Z hour did not do. It made no new low. After the 31,013.00 print at 06:40Z, price based and recovered to 31,053.25 by 07:10Z, a bounce of 49.5 points measured from the session low, against roughly 38 points off the previous low an hour earlier and roughly 20 points before that. It has since settled into a 31,035.75 to 31,053.25 band, a span of 17.5 points. A sequence in which each successive low is bought more aggressively than the last, and which then stops making lows and compresses, is mean reversion working rather than failing. The amplifier cited an hour ago, a failed retracement at 31,071.25 followed by fresh extension, did not follow through into a fourth lower low.

Tail therefore eases from 10% to 9%, mapping to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. The single point is deliberately small. It credits the halted lower-low sequence, the deepest bounce of the overnight and the 17.5-point compression, while declining to return to the 8% of the 04:00Z and 05:00Z hours, because the complex is still net lower on the session and the 31,221.25 high has not been reclaimed. Scoring this hour at 10% would ignore what the five-minute path actually did; scoring it at 7% or 8% would treat an unreclaimed high and a net-negative session as resolved.

The cross-asset read remains aligned in direction and immaterial in size. ES trades 7,766.00, down 11.25 or 0.145%, inside 7,764.00 to 7,793.00. YM trades 51,409.00, down 68.00 or 0.132%, inside 51,377.00 to 51,560.00. All three index futures are mildly negative, which is alignment of a kind, but alignment at six to fifteen basis points is not an amplifier, and no single index is leading the others lower.

Stress eases two points to 51% on genuinely new and verified evidence that the previous hour did not hold. The G7 agreed on 2 October to a coordinated release through the IEA of up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over four months, approximately 830,000 barrels per day, with substantial diesel volumes inside the first 20 days, announced by the French G7 presidency and accompanied by refinery-output commitments. Alongside reported Saudi price cuts, that is a structural supply-side de-escalator on the channel that has driven this environment. WTI has now broken below 90 at 89.835, down 1.40%, and Brent trades 101.318, down 0.91%. The 10-year eased roughly a basis point to about 5.26% in the Asian session. Stress nonetheless stays firmly elevated, and does not fall further, because none of the underlying problems has resolved: Brent remains above 100, the Strait of Hormuz remains closed with the most recent PortWatch count at a single transit and war-risk premiums reported at forty times normal, the September employment report printed 29,000 payrolls against roughly 90,000 expected with July revised down to minus 10,000 and July and August combined 60,000 lower than previously reported, unemployment at 4.2%, and a new European sovereign channel has opened, with French debt underperforming, German bund futures bid, and the euro at its weakest against the dollar since May 2025 near 1.1161 on Spanish political uncertainty. The ISM Services prices subindex at 72.6 keeps the inflation line live against a 5.24% 10-year.

Confidence improves one point to 89%, which remains high. Two material stories were verified from primary or near-primary reporting this hour that were absent from the prior assessment: the G7 and IEA release, confirmed directly from the Euronews report with the Macron statement and the four-month, 100-million-barrel, 830,000-barrel-per-day structure, and the full revision detail in the BLS Employment Situation release, including the July revision to minus 10,000. Those sit alongside a live five-minute NQ series stamped to 07:20:51Z, live ES and YM prints at 07:20:48Z and 07:20:47Z, current crude quotes, a verified Asia session wrap, and a US calendar whose release times were cross-checked against known Eastern-time conventions, with FOMC minutes at 18:00Z confirming the 14:00 Eastern mapping. The honest limits are specific. Cash VIX and cash Treasuries are closed, so the 15.31 VIX reading is a 2 October close rather than a live level, and H.15 last published 4.78% at two years and 5.24% at ten years for 1 October, a session behind the market; the roughly 5.26% 10-year is an Asian-session indicative level, not a cash print. The shared Finviz context file carries a 29 September collection timestamp, roughly 7,700 minutes old, with a partial collection status, so it was treated as unusable under the inherited 90-minute freshness rule and this assessment rests entirely on independent research.

The published path holds EA_ON across all 24 hours. It carries 9% through the European cash session, eases to an 8% floor across the 10:00Z and 11:00Z hours as European trade is assumed to mature into two-way conditions, and ticks to 9% for the 12:00Z US pre-market build. It rises to 12% for the 13:00Z hour carrying the 13:30Z cash open and the 13:45Z S&P Global composite and services finals, and to a 13% session peak for the 14:00Z hour carrying September ISM Services, consensus near 55.0 after 55.4. Those increases are scheduled-catalyst allowances, not claims about structure that cannot yet be observed. The path then decays through the US afternoon, ticks to 10% for the 19:00Z power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to a 7% floor across the assumed 21:00Z maintenance halt where no path is scoreable, and runs an 8% to 9% band through the Asian session into the European pre-open on 6 October.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding published hours are available from Claude history, and every available hour mapped to EA_ON and green with the dominant mode normal. The 06:00Z slot on 5 October is explicitly unavailable because no assessment was published inside that clock-hour; its fields are null rather than interpolated. Tail was held at 3% from 07:00Z through 21:00Z on 4 October because the CME equity-index complex was halted for the weekend and no Nasdaq-100 price path was scoreable. It then rose through the Sunday reopen as the overnight drift extended: 12% at 22:00Z, 13% at 23:00Z, 14% at 00:00Z and a 15% peak at 01:00Z on 5 October. It eased to 13% at 02:00Z once the fresh 31,221.25 high failed, to 10% at 03:00Z as the retracement completed through the prior close, and to 8% at 04:00Z and 05:00Z as that round-trip appeared to hold. Stress ran a 79% ceiling at 09:00Z on 4 October on accumulating weekend Hormuz and Gulf incident flow, eased through 73%, 70%, 68% and 66% into a 64% trough at 14:00Z as those headlines failed to transmit into crude, drifted back to 71% by 21:00Z, and then settled through 66%, 65%, 64%, 62%, 60%, 57% and 54% across the reopen hours. Confidence held a narrow 83% to 88% band, densest in the European and early US hours and thinnest across the weekend halt and the earliest reopen hours.
outlookSummary: The 07:00Z hour made no new low, and that is the hour's decisive fact. NQZ26 prints 31,041.50 at 07:20:51Z, down 0.065%, with the session low holding at 31,003.75 for roughly forty minutes. Price based at 31,013.00, recovered to 31,053.25 by 07:10Z, a 49.5-point bounce off the low against roughly 38 points an hour earlier and roughly 20 points before that, and has compressed into a 31,035.75 to 31,053.25 band spanning 17.5 points. The three-hour lower-low sequence has stopped and the 31,071.25 failed retracement did not extend into a fourth low, so Tail eases from 10% to 9%. It does not return to 8% because the complex is still net lower and the 31,221.25 high remains unretested after about six hours. ES at -0.145% and YM at -0.132% confirm alignment at six to fifteen basis points, which is not an impulse. Stress eases two points to 51% on the verified G7 and IEA coordinated release of up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel over four months agreed on 2 October, roughly 830,000 barrels per day with substantial diesel inside the first 20 days, with WTI now below 90 at 89.835 and Brent 101.318. It stays elevated because Brent holds above 100, Hormuz remains closed at roughly 1% of normal transit, the September payroll report printed +29,000 with July revised to -10,000, and a European sovereign channel has opened with French debt underperforming and the euro at its weakest since May 2025. Tail carries 9% through the European session, where 31,053.25 is the reclaim checkpoint and 31,003.75 the downside invalidation, then eases to an 8% floor across the 10:00Z and 11:00Z hours as European trade is assumed to mature. It ticks to 9% for the 12:00Z pre-market build, rises to 12% for the 13:00Z hour carrying the 13:30Z cash open and the 13:45Z S&P Global finals, and peaks at 13% for the 14:00Z hour carrying September ISM Services at a consensus near 55.0. Those are scheduled-catalyst allowances rather than observed structure. The path decays through the US afternoon, ticks to 10% for the 19:00Z power hour into the 20:00Z cash close, drops to a 7% floor across the assumed 21:00Z maintenance halt, and runs an 8% to 9% band through Asia into the European pre-open on 6 October.
